Test_Case_Description: Verify GPIO register default/reset values after power-on reset for all GPIO pad registers (GP0_GPIO_8 to GP0_GPIO_27)
Preconditions: System is powered on; GPIO block is out of reset; No prior register writes performed
Test_Steps:
1. Read each GPIO register address (GP0_GPIO_8 through GP0_GPIO_27)
2. Apply read_mask to the read data
3. Compare masked read value against expected default_value_array entry
4. Report PASS/FAIL per register
Expected_Result: All GPIO registers return their documented default/reset values. def_fail_cnt == 0
Notes: Bit[0] is masked out (data & 0xFFFFFFFE). Registers in skip_rst_array are skipped. Non-readable registers (read_mask==0) are skipped.

Test_Case_Description: Write known data patterns to all writable GPIO registers and read back to verify correctness (GP0_GPIO_8 to GP0_GPIO_27)
Preconditions: System is powered on; GPIO block is out of reset; Default value check (GPIO_TC_001) completed
Test_Steps:
1. For each of 6 data patterns (0xFFFFFFFF, 0xAAAAAAAA, 0x55555555, 0xF5F5F5F5, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xFFFF0000):
   a. Write pattern (masked with write_mask) to each GPIO register
   b. Read back each register (masked with read_mask)
   c. Compute expected value considering write_mask and read_mask
   d. Compare read value with expected value
   e. Report PASS/FAIL per register per pattern
Expected_Result: All writable GPIO registers return the expected written value after masking. wr_fail_cnt == 0 across all 6 patterns.
Notes: Registers in skip_array are skipped. Non-writable (write_mask==0) and non-readable (read_mask==0) registers are skipped. Expected value accounts for read-only bits retaining default values.

Test_Scenario: Negative Edge Interrupt Enable and Detection
Test_Case_Description: Verify that negative-edge interrupts are correctly generated and detected for each of the 32 GPIO pads (GPIO_8 to GPIO_39)
Preconditions: System is powered on; GPIO block is out of reset; GIC is initialized; SYSREG interrupt is enabled for GPIO0/GPIO1
Test_Steps:
1. Enable GIC IRQ (87 for GPIO0 or 88 for GPIO1)
2. Enable SYSREG interrupt for GPIO0/GPIO1
3. Configure all 32 GPIO pads for negative-edge interrupt (bit20=1 negedge_en, bit18=1, bit16=1)
4. For each pad i (0 to 31):
   a. Clear raw interrupt status for bit i
   b. Enable interrupt for bit i in INTR_EN1
   c. Set int_pend = 1
   d. Drive all GPIO inputs HIGH (0xFFFFFFFF)
   e. Drive GPIO input LOW for bit i (~wr_val) to create negative edge
   f. Wait for ISR (Default_IRQHandler) to clear int_pend or timeout (5000 iterations)
   g. Verify interrupt was received (no timeout)
Expected_Result: Each GPIO pad generates a negative-edge interrupt when its input transitions from HIGH to LOW. ISR fires within timeout. test_err == 0.
Registers_Tested: MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8+offset, MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1, MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1, MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1, MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1, MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1
Notes: Tests both GPIO0 and GPIO1 via compile-time #ifdef. External stimulus via address 0xA0243ffc.

Test_Scenario: Negative Edge Interrupt Status and Clearing
Test_Case_Description: Verify interrupt status register reflects correct pad and clears properly after servicing in ISR for negative-edge interrupts
Preconditions: GPIO_TC_004 preconditions met; Negative-edge interrupt triggered for a specific pad
Test_Steps:
1. In Default_IRQHandler:
   a. Read GPIO pad register - verify din bit (bit[0]) is 0 (low after negedge)
   b. Check interrupt status bit (bit[1]) is set
   c. Read group interrupt status (INTR_STS1) - verify correct bit is set
   d. Clear interrupt by writing to pad register (bit20=1, bit16=1 iclr)
   e. Clear raw interrupt status (INTR_RAW_STCLR1)
   f. Re-read group interrupt status - verify it is 0x0 (cleared)
   g. Clear SYSREG status and GIC IRQ
Expected_Result: Interrupt status correctly reflects the triggering pad. After clearing, group interrupt status reads 0x0. SYSREG and GIC are properly cleared. test_err == 0.
Notes: Validates full interrupt lifecycle: trigger -> detect -> status check -> clear -> verify cleared.

Test_Scenario: Positive Edge Interrupt Enable and Detection for All Pads
Test_Case_Description: Verify that positive-edge interrupts are correctly generated and detected for all 32 GPIO pads simultaneously (GPIO_8 to GPIO_39)
Preconditions: System is powered on; GPIO block is out of reset; GIC is initialized; SYSREG interrupt is enabled for GPIO0/GPIO1
Test_Steps:
1. Enable GIC IRQ (87 for GPIO0 or 88 for GPIO1)
2. Enable SYSREG interrupt for GPIO0/GPIO1
3. Configure all 32 GPIO pads for positive-edge interrupt (bit17=1 posedge_en via 0x00020000)
4. Set IO control groups 1-4 for input mode (doe=1, value 0x000000FF)
5. Enable all 32 interrupts in INTR_EN1 (0xFFFFFFFF)
6. For each pad i (0 to 31):
   a. Drive all GPIO inputs LOW (0x00000000)
   b. Set int_pend = 1 (arm before edge)
   c. Drive all GPIO inputs HIGH (0xFFFFFFFF) to create rising edge
   d. Wait for ISR (Default_IRQHandler) to clear int_pend or timeout (2000 iterations)
   e. Verify interrupt was received (no timeout)
   f. Drive LOW again to prepare for next iteration
Expected_Result: Each GPIO pad generates a positive-edge interrupt when input transitions from LOW to HIGH. ISR fires within timeout for all 32 pads. test_err == 0.
Notes: Tests all 32 pads in sequence. External stimulus via address 0xA0243ffc. IO control groups configured for input mode.

Test_Scenario: Positive Edge Group Interrupt Status and Clearing
Test_Case_Description: Verify group interrupt status register reflects correct state and clears properly after servicing in ISR for positive-edge interrupts on all pads
Preconditions: GPIO_TC_006 preconditions met; Positive-edge interrupt triggered
Test_Steps:
1. In Default_IRQHandler:
   a. Read group interrupt status (INTR_STS1) - verify non-zero (interrupt raised)
   b. Disable group interrupt (write 0x0 to INTR_EN1) during service
   c. Clear per-pin raw status for all 32 pads (write 0x00010000 iclr to each pad register)
   d. Wait 2 cycles
   e. Re-read group interrupt status - verify it is 0x0 (cleared)
   f. Clear SYSREG status register and verify it is cleared
   g. Re-enable group interrupt (write 0xFFFFFFFF to INTR_EN1)
   h. Clear GIC IRQ
Expected_Result: Group interrupt status is non-zero when interrupt occurs. After clearing all per-pin statuses, group status reads 0x0. SYSREG status is cleared. test_err == 0.
Notes: Validates full group interrupt lifecycle for posedge: trigger -> group status check -> per-pin clear -> group verify -> sysreg clear -> re-enable.
